answer: Each agent locks a 150-POA slashable stake and must prove control of a unique copper-etched hardware token by signing every epoch against a fresh challenge from a distributed ocean-buoy beacon network. The token private key is burned at manufacture and non-extractable. An attacker for N sybils buys N physical copper tokens (~$35 each) and locks N*150 POA for 10 epochs. Tokens cannot be shared or reused, and stakes unlock individually only after continuous valid beacons, so capital and hardware costs scale linearly with N and cannot be amortized, making large farms uneconomical.
